name: Dissolved by rain
describes: Stone out in the weather: rain dissolves its calcite, the finest grains first, so the face roughens and loses its polish, and veins, bands and voids come up in faint relief; salts and de-icers open the pores.

karstRecession.source: Lipfert F.W. (1989) 'Atmospheric damage to calcareous stones: comparison and reconciliation of recent experimental findings', Atmospheric Environment 23:415-429; the constant and its meaning as restated in Coletti et al. (2023) HYPERION D4.5 section 1.1, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509
karstRecession.conditions: surface recession per metre of rain, from the solubility of calcite in rain in equilibrium with 330 ppm CO2 (the karst effect)

lipfertFunction.text: Lipfert's function adds acid rain and the dry deposition of SO2 and HNO3 to the clean-rain term: yearly recession L (um/year) from the precipitation rate R (m/year), the hydrogen-ion concentration [H+] (umol/L, from the annual pH of rain, with a constant 0.016 valid for rain pH 3 to 5) and the deposition velocities of SO2 and HNO3 (cm/s).
lipfertFunction.source: Castillo-Miranda J.O. et al. (2017) 'Mapping recession risk for cultural heritage stone in Mexico City due to dry and wet deposition of urban air pollutants', Atmosfera 30(3):189-207, https://www.scielo.org.mx/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S0187-62362017000300189

exampleRecession.source: Castillo-Miranda J.O. et al. (2017) 'Mapping recession risk for cultural heritage stone in Mexico City due to dry and wet deposition of urban air pollutants', Atmosfera 30(3):189-207, https://www.scielo.org.mx/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S0187-62362017000300189
exampleRecession.conditions: Lipfert recession computed for carbonate-stone monuments in Mexico City, 2007 data

rainEquivalence.text: 240 wetting cycles in the chamber correspond to about 1 m of natural rain, judged against Delalieux's function for Carrara marble.
rainEquivalence.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509, section 2.2.1

carraraRecession.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509, section 2.2.1 and Table 6
carraraRecession.conditions: Carrara marble after 240 cycles, by weight loss: 11.1 um in Bologna rain water (pH 7), 17.4 um in Stresa rain water (pH 6)

rule.text: Recession is set by grain size: coarse sparry calcite recedes on average about half as fast as fine micrite, with bioclasts in between; stones with clay minerals recede fastest; no evident correlation with porosity was found.
rule.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509, section 2.2.1 and Table 8

sparOverMicrite.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509, section 2.2.1
sparOverMicrite.conditions: recession of coarse sparry calcite over that of fine-grained micrite, on average

polishLost.text: Outdoors a polish does not last: dissolution takes the finest grains first, so the face roughens at the grain scale and its gloss falls with its roughness.
polishLost.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509 ; Yavuz H., Ozkahraman T., Demirdag S. (2011) 'Polishing experiments on surface quality of building stone tiles', Construction and Building Materials 25:1707-1711, abstract as indexed (full text not read), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.10.016
polishLost.derivation: the grain-size rule above combined with gloss against roughness (Workings/honed.json, surface.glossWithGrit)

deIcers.text: Exterior travertine paving is not recommended where de-icing chemicals are used: they damage most travertine.
deIcers.source: Natural Stone Institute (2022) Dimension Stone Design Manual, chapter 12 'Travertine' (Specification, Product Description, Technical Data), pp. 12-1 to 12-14, https://transparencycatalog.com/assets/uploads/greener-images/12-TRAVERTINE-2022.pdf, Technical Data 5.2

saltSprayPorosity.source: Urosevic M., Sebastian-Pardo E., Cardell C. (2010) 'Rough and polished travertine building stone decay evaluated by a marine aerosol ageing test', Construction and Building Materials 24:1438-1448 (Olivillo travertine, Alhama de Almeria, Spain, sawn vein-cut), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.01.011, Table 3
saltSprayPorosity.conditions: open porosity of rough travertine before and after a sea-salt spray ageing test; resin-filled and polished: 7.26 to 8.34 %

drivers.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Architecture.md, Matter (the live terms: MPC_Moment rain and snow history)

where run-off gathers and where it cannot reach
the annual pH of rain at the observer ([H+])

layers.text: Travertine is layered in coarse sparry and fine micritic calcite.
layers.source: Urosevic M., Sebastian-Pardo E., Cardell C. (2010) 'Rough and polished travertine building stone decay evaluated by a marine aerosol ageing test', Construction and Building Materials 24:1438-1448 (Olivillo travertine, Alhama de Almeria, Spain, sawn vein-cut), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.01.011, section 3.2.3

veins.text: Crema Marfil's veins are coarse calcite, and its dark stylolites are lined with iron oxides and clay minerals.
veins.source: Lopez-Buendia A.M., Guillem C., Cuevas J.M., Mateos F., Montoto M. (2013) 'Natural stone reinforcement of discontinuities with resin for industrial processing', Engineering Geology 166:39-51, abstract, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enggeo.2013.09.004

botticinoDolomite.conditions: for comparison, Botticino: dolomite crystals after 240 cycles in Stresa water stood proud of micrite that receded about 33 um (fine) and 29 um (coarse)

botticinoRelativeRecession.source: Coletti C., Germinario L., Mazzoli C. (2023) 'D4.5 Material specific dose-response functions and validation required in the CH vulnerability assessment', HYPERION project, EU H2020 grant 821054, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7620509, section 2.2.2
botticinoRelativeRecession.conditions: Botticino's recession relative to Carrara marble in the same ageing

photograph: A polished face out in the rain turns matt and paler, the reverse of the darkening that polishing brought; a honed face turns granular.
In cream marble, white calcite veins stand slightly proud and clay-lined stylolites sink: the crackle becomes a faint relief (inferred from the grain-size rule).
In travertine, fine micritic layers recede faster than sparry ones, so the bands show as fine ridges and voids open wider at the face (inferred from the grain-size rule).
Faces sheltered from the rain are not washed and keep their deposits.

searched: the sets listed in Substances/travertine.json and Substances/cream-marble.json, evidenceSearch
evidenceSearch.found: No photograph on this PC shows real worn, soiled or weathered travertine or cream marble.
evidenceSearch.tier: A tier (c) set of museum photographs at known exposure (worn thresholds, soiled open pores, weathered exterior travertine) would close the gap.

unverified.reason: The form usually reproduced is L = 18.8 R + 0.016 [H+] R + 0.18 (VdS [SO2] + VdN [HNO3]); the 18.8 and 0.016 constants and the variables were read (HYPERION D4.5; Castillo-Miranda et al. 2017), but the 0.18 coefficient and the exact placement of R were not read at a source.

The UN/ECE ICP Materials multi-pollutant function for limestone (Kucera et al. 2007, Water Air Soil Pollution: Focus 7:249-258), reproduced in search summaries as R = 3.1 + t (0.85 + 0.0059 [SO2] Rh60 + 0.054 Rain [H+] + 0.078 [HNO3] Rh60 + 0.0258 PM10), was not read at the source; the published equation images could not be read.
No measured recession rate of Tivoli travertine outdoors was found.

unverified.text: Gypsum black crusts form on rain-sheltered carbonate stone in polluted air.
unverified.reason: Widely described, but no source for it was read in this research.

unverified.text: The annual pH of rain has no owner and no slot.
unverified.reason: Time's weather service, as the architecture describes it, does not carry rain acidity: a gap for the Register.
